---
title: "Gradient Reconstruction"
description: "Estimating cell-centred gradients on unstructured finite volume meshes."
categories: [Theory, finite volume]
---

In a cell-centred finite volume method the solution is stored as one value per cell, but many terms
in the discretized equations (diffusive fluxes on non-orthogonal meshes, higher-order convection
schemes, source terms) need the gradient of that field. Gradient reconstruction is the process of
estimating $\nabla \phi$ at each cell centre from the values in that cell and its neighbours.

## Green-Gauss {#sec-green-gauss}

Applying the divergence theorem over a control volume $P$ with volume $V_P$ gives

$$
\nabla \phi_P \approx \frac{1}{V_P} \sum_{f} \phi_f \, \mathbf{S}_f,
$$ {#eq-green-gauss}

where $\phi_f$ is the value interpolated to face $f$ and $\mathbf{S}_f$ is the outward face area vector.
The accuracy of @eq-green-gauss depends heavily on how $\phi_f$ is obtained.

## Least squares {#sec-least-squares}

The least-squares approach instead chooses $\nabla \phi_P$ to minimize the weighted error in a
first-order Taylor expansion to each neighbour $k$:

$$
\min_{\nabla \phi_P} \sum_{k} w_k \left( \phi_k - \phi_P - \nabla \phi_P \cdot \mathbf{d}_k \right)^2,
$$ {#eq-least-squares}

where $\mathbf{d}_k$ is the vector from the centre of $P$ to the centre of neighbour $k$. Compare
this with the Green-Gauss approach in @sec-green-gauss.
